# Introduction

Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria syndrome (HGPS) is a rare genetic disorder associated with accelerated aging. This project examines whether age is associated with gene-expression variation among skin fibroblast samples collected from individuals with HGPS.
The dataset is GEO accession GSE206684 and contains 11 human skin fibroblast RNA seq samples. 


# Dataset and sample metadata

The raw gene-count files are stored in `samples/R-transcriptomes/`. Each file contains gene identifiers and raw read counts.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

required_packages <- c(
  "edgeR", "ggplot2", "AnnotationDbi", "Homo.sapiens"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following packages before knitting: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

library(edgeR)
library(ggplot2)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(Homo.sapiens)
```

## Import raw count data

```{r import-counts}
files <- list.files(
  "samples/R-transcriptomes",
  pattern = "^GSM626.*\\.tsv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

files <- sort(files)

if (length(files) != 11) {
  stop(
    "Expected 11 GSM626*.tsv count files, but found ",
    length(files),
    ". Check the data directory and filenames."
  )
}

count_list <- lapply(files, function(file) {
  data <- read.delim(
    file,
    header = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  colnames(data) <- c("Gene", basename(file))
  data
})

same_gene_order <- vapply(
  count_list,
  function(x) identical(x$Gene, count_list[[1]]$Gene),
  logical(1)
)

if (!all(same_gene_order)) {
  stop("The gene identifiers or their order differ among count files.")
}

counts <- do.call(cbind, lapply(count_list, function(x) x[[2]]))
rownames(counts) <- count_list[[1]]$Gene
colnames(counts) <- sub("_.*", "", basename(files))

dim(counts)
head(counts[, 1:3])
```

The resulting count matrix should contain 26,369 rows (gene identifiers) and 11 columns (samples) before filtering.

## Sample metadata

```{r metadata}
metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(counts),
  cell_line = c(
    "NA01178", "NA01972", "NG01178", "NG03198", "NG06917",
    "NG07493", "NG08466", "NG10578", "NG10677", "NG11513",
    "NG11572"
  ),
  age = c(20, 14, 20, 10, 3, 2, 8, 17, 4, 8, 2),
  sex = c(
    "Male", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male",
    "Female", "Female", "Male", "Male", "Female", "Female"
  ),
  genotype = rep("HGPS", 11),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rownames(metadata) <- metadata$sample
metadata$sex <- factor(metadata$sex)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(metadata), colnames(counts)))

metadata
summary(metadata$age)
table(metadata$sex)
```

There are 11 samples, with ages ranging from 2 to 20 years. The sample set includes six female and five male individuals.

# Expression filtering and normalization

The edgeR workflow is used to filter lowly expressed genes, normalize library sizes, estimate dispersion, and fit a quasi-likelihood generalized linear model.

```{r filtering-normalization}
y <- DGEList(counts = counts)

design <- model.matrix(~ age + sex, data = metadata)

keep <- filterByExpr(y, design = design)
y <- y[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]

y <- calcNormFactors(y)

dim(y)
```

The number of genes remaining after filtering is reported above. The filtered and normalized data are used for both PCA and differential-expression analysis.

# Principal component analysis

Principal component analysis (PCA) is used to explore variation in gene expression among samples. The plots show samples colored by age and by sex.

```{r pca}
logCPM <- cpm(y, log = TRUE, prior.count = 2)

pca <- prcomp(
  t(logCPM),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

percentVar <- pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100

pca_data <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(pca$x),
  PC1 = pca$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca$x[, 2],
  age = metadata$age[match(rownames(pca$x), metadata$sample)],
  sex = metadata$sex[match(rownames(pca$x), metadata$sample)]
)

pca_age_plot <- ggplot(
  pca_data,
  aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = age)
) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sample), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of HGPS Skin Fibroblast Gene Expression",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(percentVar[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(percentVar[2], 1), "%)"),
    color = "Age (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

pca_sex_plot <- ggplot(
  pca_data,
  aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = sex)
) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sample), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of HGPS Samples by Sex",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(percentVar[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(percentVar[2], 1), "%)"),
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

pca_age_plot
pca_sex_plot

ggsave(
  "Lab11_PCA_Age.png",
  plot = pca_age_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

ggsave(
  "Lab11_PCA_Sex.png",
  plot = pca_sex_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

round(percentVar[1:5], 2)
```

PC1 explains approximately **28.52%** of the variance and PC2 explains approximately **19.25%**. Together, the first two components explain approximately **47.77%** of the total variance. The PCA plots are exploratory and should be interpreted in the context of the small sample size.

# Differential-expression analysis

A quasi-likelihood generalized linear model is fitted using age and sex as predictors. The age coefficient tests the association between age and gene expression while accounting for sex.

```{r differential-expression}
y <- estimateDisp(y, design, robust = TRUE)

fit <- glmQLFit(y, design, robust = TRUE)

qlf_age <- glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "age")

age_results <- topTags(qlf_age, n = Inf)$table
age_results$Gene <- rownames(age_results)

summary(decideTests(qlf_age))

nrow(age_results)

head(age_results, 20)
```

# Human gene annotation

Gene symbols are mapped to Entrez Gene identifiers and full gene names using the `Homo.sapiens` annotation package.

```{r annotation}
gene_symbols <- unique(age_results$Gene)

entrez_ids <- mapIds(
  Homo.sapiens,
  keys = gene_symbols,
  column = "ENTREZID",
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

gene_names <- mapIds(
  Homo.sapiens,
  keys = gene_symbols,
  column = "GENENAME",
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

age_results$ENTREZID <- entrez_ids[age_results$Gene]
age_results$GENENAME <- gene_names[age_results$Gene]

annotation_summary <- data.frame(
  Total_Genes = nrow(age_results),
  Mapped_Genes = sum(!is.na(age_results$ENTREZID)),
  Unmapped_Genes = sum(is.na(age_results$ENTREZID)),
  Percent_Mapped = round(
    mean(!is.na(age_results$ENTREZID)) * 100,
    2
  )
)

annotation_summary
head(age_results, 20)
```

In the final analysis, 13,284 of 14,499 genes mapped to Entrez identifiers, corresponding to 91.62% of the tested genes.

## Export results

```{r export-results}
write.csv(
  age_results,
  "Lab11_Age_Differential_Expression_Annotated.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  age_results[, c("Gene", "logFC", "logCPM", "F", "PValue", "FDR")],
  "Lab11_Age_Differential_Expression.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  annotation_summary,
  "Lab11_Annotation_Summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

file.exists(c(
  "Lab11_Age_Differential_Expression_Annotated.csv",
  "Lab11_Age_Differential_Expression.csv",
  "Lab11_Annotation_Summary.csv",
  "Lab11_PCA_Age.png",
  "Lab11_PCA_Sex.png"
))
```

# Interpretation and conclusion

A total of 14,499 genes passed the expression filter. Differential expression analysis was performed using an edgeR linear model, with age and sex included as predictors. The age coefficient was used to identify genes associated with age while accounting for sex.
No genes were statistically significant at an FDR threshold of 0.05. But several genes had small unadjusted p-values, none significant after correction for multiple testing. These results did not establish that age has no relationship with gene expression. Rather, the small sample size of 11 individuals may have limited the ability to detect age-associated changes.
Because all samples were obtained from individuals with HGPS, this analysis evaluates age-associated gene expression within the HGPS group and does not compare HGPS samples with healthy controls. 

# Limitations

- The dataset contains only 11 samples,  limits statistical power.
- All samples are from individuals with HGPS, no healthy control group.
- The age distribution and sex composition are not  balanced.
- PCA is descriptive
- Gene annotation may be incomplete for some.
